digest.component_or_area: reconciler backend adapter seam and architecture documentation
propositions: ADR 0035 section 6 states the first real second backend is out of scope, but epic e369 lands Jira Data Center as the second backend ahead of the GitHub adapter, requiring three sites in ADR 0035 to be corrected (diagram comment :111, prose :204-205, Decision item 6 :236-237, and Consequences section).

TicketTransport declares six members but the reconciler calls twenty-one distinct transport methods, with twelve absent from DC implementation and unaware to any Protocol, causing a silent runtime crash on set_entity_property despite passing isinstance checks and 1636 unit tests.

RemoteRef.instance is presented as a distinguishing mechanism for deployments but is never constructed in production code (grep returns nothing on src/), only in two test helpers, creating a gap between the stated design and implementation.

The backend contract suite certifies a backend only if the port is complete and typed; unannotated transport parameters make port incompleteness invisible to mypy, requiring structural tests rather than authorial discipline.

docs/user-guide.md must document DC least-privilege security (dedicated PAT scoped to reconciled projects only, never admin token), allow_insecure cleartext-only-if-you-must, ca_bundle for internal-CA certificates, and resolved_statuses for custom workflows.

The jira_family sub-seam is shared between Jira Data Center and future backends through dependency inversion via location-pinned modules (adf.py, outbound_fields.py, comment_limits.py), with March 2029 as the DC read-only date making this a deliberately time-boxed investment.
